title: [C10T1] - Australian household energy use and emissions
prompt: The first chart below shows how energy is used in an average Australian household. The second chart shows the greenhouse gas emissions which result from this energy use. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features and making comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The pie charts illustrate the proportion of energy consumption and the corresponding greenhouse gas emissions in an average Australian household across six different categories.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, heating shows the most striking difference between the two charts, being the highest energy consumer but contributing a considerably smaller proportion to greenhouse gas emissions. Meanwhile, water heating represents the largest share of emissions and comes second in energy use, with relatively similar proportions across energy use and emissions.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding the major energy consumers, heating leads energy use at a significant 42%, yet produces far fewer emissions at merely 15%, demonstrating a dramatic disparity of 27 percentage points. Meanwhile, water heating comes second in household energy use, accounting for 30%, and contributes 32% to greenhouse gas emissions, showing relatively similar proportions. At the same time, other appliances consume a moderate 15% of energy while generating nearly double that proportion in emissions, at a considerable 28%, representing the second-largest share of greenhouse gas production, after water heating.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: As for the remaining categories, refrigeration accounts for a modest 7% of energy use but a notably higher 14% of emissions, exactly doubling its environmental impact. Moreover, lighting maintains relatively minor proportions at 4% for energy consumption and 8% for emissions. Finally, cooling represents the smallest energy consumer at a negligible 2%, while producing a slightly higher 3% of greenhouse gas emissions.
